articleTitle: A Novel Voltage Sag Detection Method for Series Filter Originate from Improved Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: With the access of a large number of distributed wind and solar new energy to the power grid, the power quality problem becomes more and more prominent due to the power conversion characteristics of its power electronics. Voltage sags is the most serious problems in the power industry of power quality. Series filters can effectively compensate for voltage sags and other voltage quality problems, and are important governance equipment to solve power quality problems in distribution networks. In this paper, a series filter voltage sag detection algorithm originate from improved immune genetic algorithm is proposed. The core of the algorithm is to decouple crosslink among dq axes of the series filter to improve performance of control. The algorithm of this paper is used to optimize the controller parameters. While solving the blindness and randomness of the general genetic algorithm, the PI controller parameters are optimized with fast response and strong robustness, which solves the problem that the controller parameters are difficult to adapt to the changing environment. Finally, the UPQC simulation model considering microgrid is established, and it is verified that the method can accurately detect and compensate voltage dips in microgrid. The real-time performance is good and the voltage compensation performance is improved.

articleTitle: A Multi-Service Real-Time Resource Scheduling Optimization Method Based on the O-RAN Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: The Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) has emerged as a key architecture to address diverse service demands and resource allocation challenges due to its openness and intelligence. However, traditional algorithms struggle to balance quality of service (QoS) and energy optimization in dynamic, high-dimensional environments. This paper proposes an O-RAN resource allocation method combining latent space modeling with the Actor-Critic framework. Offline latent space enhancement extracts features from historical data, while reinforcement learning optimizes resource allocation policies for efficient online decision-making. Experimental results show superior performance in cumulative rewards, QoS satisfaction, and energy optimization, with remarkable stability and adaptability under dynamic loads, providing an efficient and scalable solution for next-generation wireless networks.

articleTitle: A Simple π-Shaped Printed Microstrip Filtering Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: In this paper, a π-shaned printing monopole antenna with a total antenna size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{24\times 28\times 0.544\ mm^{3}}$</tex> is introduced. The radial antenna is improved from T shape to Π shape. The T-shape operates at 6.11 ~ 6.26GHz, and the improved π shape operates at 6.11 ~ 6.28GHz. The voltage standing wave ratio is improved from 1.17:1 to 1.04:1. The peak gain of the antenna is improved from 1.70dBi to 1.89dBi, and the radiation efficiency of the antenna is improved from 92% to 99%.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Broadband Electromagnetic Wave Absorbing Metamaterials Based on Graphene
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This paper proposes a reconfigurable broadband electromagnetic wave absorbing metamaterial based on graphene. By employing a cascaded resonance structure composed of multilayer patterned resistive films, broadband electromagnetic absorption is achieved. To enable reconfigurable electromagnetic properties, graphene is incorporated into the metamaterial structure. The impedance of graphene, adjustable via voltage bias, allows active control of the absorption performance of the metamaterial. Simulation results indicate that the designed absorbing metamaterial achieves a minimum absorption rate of 90% within the frequency range of 1.32 GHz to 20 GHz, corresponding to a relative bandwidth of 175.2%. The profile thickness is only 0.11λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, and the design exhibits polarization insensitivity and excellent incident angle stability. Furthermore, by tuning the sheet resistance of graphene, the minimum absorption rate can be actively adjusted from 90% to 35%. This absorbing metamaterial has broad applications in stealth technology, enabling electromagnetic camouflage and deception in different electromagnetic scattering backgrounds.

articleTitle: Research on Conversion Matrix and Optimal Polarization Angle of Radar Oblique Polarization Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: When radar detects targets, different polarization modes and parameters have different effects on target detection. In order to study the influence of the change of polarization angle on RCS in oblique polarization detection, a transformation matrix from horizontal polarization to oblique polarization at any angle is proposed. The relationship between horizontal/vertical polarization scattering matrix and oblique polarization scattering matrix can be derived through this matrix, and the oblique polarization RCS is expressed as a function of oblique polarization angle. The maximum value of the function is solved and the optimal detection polarization angle is determined.

articleTitle: Super-Resolution Confocal Scanning Imaging with Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: Metasurface-based imaging is a promising technology due to its low hardware cost and system complexity. However, the resolution is very limited due to its small aperture size and long carrier wavelength. To improve the resolution of metasurface-based imaging, we propose a two-step deconvolution based on a confocal scanning imaging system. First, we develop a focal plane scanning imaging system with confocal configuration to provide enough SNR. Meanwhile, the highly focused beam can be measured to get the point spread function (PSF). Next, regularized deconvolution with sparse and total variation (TV) prior is applied to denoise and improve the resolution slightly. Finally, we apply Richardson-Lucy (RL) deconvolution to further improve the resolution. Both simulations and experiments demonstrate the proposed method can greatly improve the resolution and contrast of the imaging results.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Miniaturized Dual-Polarization Square Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: A novel design for a miniaturized dual-polarized square patch antenna with high-gain is presented. The formation of a simple array with the radiating patches enables the achievement of high gain. In order to reduce the number of feed ports, the antenna employs a coupling feeding technique for excitation, thereby achieving miniaturization through the bending and layering of the feed arms. Activation of different feed ports enables the antenna to operate in either vertical polarization (VP) or horizontal polarization (HP). The measured bandwidth (SII < -15 dB) of the proposed antenna is 875 MHz to 930 MHz, with port isolation exceeding 25 dB across this frequency range. The measured maximum gain of the proposed antenna is 9.43 dBi (VP) and 9.46 dBi (HP), and the cross-polarization ratio is above 20 dB in the main radiation direction, indicating robust radiation performance.

articleTitle: Joint Beamforming Design Based on Graph Neural Convection Diffusion Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS), as an emerging green communication technology, improves the communication quality of wireless communication networks by reconfiguring the wireless propagation environment. This paper focuses on IRS-assisted multiple input single output wireless communication systems, considering the j oint optimization of transmission beamforming at the Access Point (AP) and reflection beamforming of passive phase shifters at the IRS under the constraint of total transmission power at the AP to maximize the sum rate of the users. To solve the nonconvex optimization problem of multivariable coupling, this paper develops a graph neural convection diffusion model based on the convection diffusion equation to solve the joint beamforming design. The experimental results show that under the same conditions, the proposed algorithm achieves a larger sum rate of users compared to other algorithms, demonstrating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Geometric Morphological Analysis Method for Sediment Based on Dynamic Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: To precisely delineate the three-dimensional morphological features of sediment particles, this research has proposed a calculation approach for geometric morphological parameters of sediment particles based on dynamic image processing technology. This method has implemented the marking of trajectories of moving sediment particles using the Matlab programming language and computed the three-axis morphological parameters such as the long axis, median axis, and short axis of the particles, as well as the sphericity. The results indicated that the sediment particles in the source area of the Yangtze River are mainly composed of coarse sand, fine gravel, and medium gravel. These particles present remarkable irregularity in morphology, a distinct non-spherical tendency, and a preference for flattening and elongation in three-dimensional space. This study has overcome the limitation that traditional sediment geometric morphology analysis has to rely on direct physical measurement and has achieved a precise, efficient, and non-destructive quantitative description of the morphological characteristics of sediment particles.

articleTitle: Research on Filter Transmission Performance Based on Substrate Stacking Process
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: Aiming at the impedance matching problem when RF transmission lines are cascaded with RF devices and the parasitic effect of bandpass filter chips in the vertical interconnection structure of the substrate, a solution to match the bonding connection between the bandpass lines and the filter chips in the chip stacking process is proposed. An electromagnetic simulation model is developed to analyze the influence of key parameters and copper laying structure on the transmission performance. The optimized chip cascade structure has good VSWR and transmission performance in the operating frequency band, and at the same time brings higher out-of-band suppression, which provides a reference for practical circuit applications.

articleTitle: Vector Mixer Characterization with True Calibration Kit Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This paper presents the use of non-ideal calibration kits to enhance calibration accuracy, with a particular focus on Vector Mixer Calibration techniq ues. We present the true param-eters of load in the calibration kit, replacing the assumption of an ideal load. This approach reduces the residual error by utilizing a comprehensive Short-Open-Load (SOL) calibration equation. The Vector Mixer Calibration technique characterizes the parameters of mixer-filter combinations that meet the reciprocal condition using the reflection method. Incorporating the real parameters of the load during the calibration process improves the accuracy of cali-bration mixer characterization. Measurement results confirm that the proposed calibration method achieves high accuracy in mixer measurements.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Dual-polarization Switchable Active Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: Based on PIN diodes, a broadband dual-polarized active frequency selective surface (AFSS) with switchable operating modes is designed in this paper. Three metal layers are sandwiched between two F4B substrates to form the model. Four PIN diodes are placed on the metal layer to enable the switching function between reflection and transmission modes. Moreover, the interaction of the metal layers produces second-order resonance, significantly enhancing the transmission bandwidth. When the AFSS operates in the reflection mode, electromagnetic (EM) waves are completely shielded from 0 to 8.24 GHz. In the transmission mode, the transmission bandwidth ranges from 2.96 to 4.6 GHz, and the relative bandwidth is 43.4%. The structure's equivalent circuit model (ECM) is proposed, and the switching principle of AFSS is analyzed based on this. The simulated results show that the AFSS achieves a dual-polarized wideband switching function and maintains stability for EM waves at a 30° oblique incidence, indicating its great potential in stealth technology.

articleTitle: High-Selectivity Bandpass Filter with Controllable Transmission Zeros Designed Using an Over-Moded Groove Gap Waveguide Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: In this paper, based on the gap waveguide technology, an X-band high-selectivity and low-loss over-moded filter with out-of-band transmission zero point is proposed. The filter has good electrical performance and manufacturing flexibility, which can reduce manufacturing costs. It consists of two cascade cavities designed using a grooved gap waveguide structure. It consists of two cascaded cavities designed using the groove gap waveguide structure. By adjusting the structure and size, it can flexibly control the position of the two transmission zero points in the upper and lower stop bands. The design has very good out-of-band suppression and simple structure. To validate this structure, a filter was designed and optimized, operating in the X-band with a center frequency of 11.1 GHz. It has two out-of-band transmission zeros, with a passband bandwidth of approximately 100 MHz. The maximum in-band return loss is 30 dB, and the minimum insertion loss is 0.4 dB.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility Design of Angle Sensor for Rubber-Tired Train
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the electromagnetic compatibility design of an angle sensor for a certain type of rubber-tired train. It addresses the issue of sensor signal cables being susceptible to crosstalk from high-voltage power cables by adding a shielding layer to the cables and grounding it to shield against electromagnetic interference. After grounding the shielding layer at two points, the tested signals still exhibit significant errors. The cause of this is the high-frequency common-mode voltage generated by the train's inverter system, which flows into the train body and creates a potential difference. The common-mode current then flows into the shielding layer through the grounding points and couples into the signal cables. The grounding method of the sensor cable for axis 1 was modified, changing from dual-point grounding to single-point grounding. After the modification, the common-mode current no longer flows into the shielding layer. Testing results show that the signal error meets the requirements. Under the electromagnetic environment of the train, single-point grounding provides a better electromagnetic compatibility effect.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Pulse Damage Study of Low-noise Amplifier Module for Navigation Receiver Front-End
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This paper investigates the voltage damage threshold and main damage types of the low-noise amplifier (LNA) module in the front-end of UAV receivers through high-altitude nuclear electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) equivalent injection experiments. Conduct electromagnetic pulse injection experiments by using EFT equivalent HEMP waveform. By designing experiments, compare the insertion loss (S21) and return loss (S11) of LNA modules before and after injecting electromagnetic pulses with different voltage amplitudes, and analyze the damage voltage threshold and damage type of LNA modules. After analyzing and organizing the experimental data, it was found that the damage types of the LNA module were related to the amplitude of the injection voltage. The main damage types were degraded LNA signal amplification function (injection voltage of 1500-2000V), transistor short circuit (injection voltage of 2000-2250V), and transistor open circuit (injection voltage higher than 2250V). This paper enriches the study of electromagnetic damage effects on the front end of UAV receivers, and provides a reference for the study of electromagnetic protection of UAV receivers or EMP weapons.

articleTitle: A 60GHz Variable Gain Phase Shifter with 9-Bit Phase Resolution for Phased Array in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This paper presents a 60GHz variable gain phase shifter (VGPS) with 9-bit phase resolution in 65nm CMOS technology for phased array. The proposed phase shifter is realized by employing liner phase control technique and a wideband in-phase /quadrature (I/Q) network. The simulated 3-dB bandwidth is 47-65GHz. By current reusing and gain control technology, the gain of VGPS is -27 to -4.6dB and the root-mean-square phase error is below 0.34°. This chip consumes 14.5 mA from a 1-V voltage supply and the core of the phase shifter is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$560\text{um}\times 610\text{um}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A 2.5-Dimensional Frequency Selective Sensor for Detecting Strain Magnitude and Direction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: In the past decade, there have been numerous potential applications for Frequency selective surface (FSS) based sensors. A new 2.5-dimensional (2.5D) FSS sensor design is proposed for strain sensing in this work. The proposed FSS unit cell is composed of multiple metal wires and dielectric layers, and metallic blind via holes are used to connect the metal wires between the different layers. Compared to the conventional single-layer dipole unit cell, the proposed multi-layer FSS structure can significantly reduce the unit cell size. The simulation results show that the FSS sensor's resonance frequency decreases from 14.996 GHz to 14.379 GHz as the horizontal strain increases from 0% to 4%. The FSS sensor's resonance frequency increases from 14.996 GHz to 15.192 GHz as the vertical strain increases from 0% to 4%. The sensitivities of the FSS sensor in the horizontal direction and vertical direction are −15.425 kHz/microstrain and 4.9 kHz/microstrain, respectively. Due to the FSS sensor's resonance frequency shift direction and the value of sensitivity are different in the two strain directions, the magnitude and direction of the strain can be quantitatively detected by the proposed FSS sensor.

articleTitle: A Noise Circulating VCO with Switch-Coupled Inductors Achieving Linearized Kvco for Sub-6G Communication Applications in 22nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This paper presents a noise circulating VCO with switch-coupled inductors achieving linearized Kvco for Sub-6G communication applications in a 22nm CMOS technology. The switch-coupled inductors are utilized to enable VCO operate in different modes for achieving wide frequency coverage without significantly impacting phase noise. NMOS and PMOS varactors are employed to make the variation amplitude of Kvco smaller, which results in a lineared Kvco. The exhibits a wide tuning range from 19.8 to 23.7GHz, achieving a 17.9% tuning range. It has exhibited a phase noise of -110.8dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset from the 19.8 GHz carrier frequency and consumes 6.8 mW of power.

articleTitle: A Three-Dimensional Broadband Absorbing Structure Based on Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: In this paper, a three-dimensional broadband strongly absorbing absorber is proposed, which achieves broadband matching performance by combining the three-dimensional impedance tapering resistive films and a two-dimensional circular resistive film. After simulation design and optimization, the reflection coefficient is better than −20 dB in the range of 2–18 GHz, and in particular, there are strong absorption peaks at 2.3 GHz and 8.0 GHz, with the absorption peak at 8 GHz reaching −55 dB. When the electromagnetic incident changes from 0° to 50°, the absorption is more than 90% in the range of 1.8-18 GHz, with a good polarization uniformity.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on the Electromagnetic Damage Effects of the Gyroscope System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: The gyroscope system is a crucial component of the inertial navigation system in drones and is susceptible to the effects of electromagnetic pulses (EMP). Therefore, an analysis of the circuit principles of the gyroscope system is conducted firstly, and the gyroscope system is taking as the research object. Pulse current injection experiments are conducted on both the signal output port and the power supply port to investigate the electromagnetic damage effects on the gyroscope system under the influence of electromagnetic pulses. Research indicates that the signal port is more susceptible to electromagnetic pulse (EMP) effects compared to the power supply port. PCI tests reveal that when the actual injected current at the signal output port reaches 15 A, it experiences electromagnetic damage, resulting in a loss of data transmission capability.

articleTitle: Area-Selective Microwave Heating in Cylindrical Cavity Based on Phased Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: Area-selective microwave heating will influence the future of modulating heating. However, the existing area-selective microwave heating system is complex and the process is cumbersome. This paper presents a phased antenna array setting in a cylindrical cavity, achieving area-selective microwave heating. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed phased antenna array have the ability of independent area-selective heating in cylindrical cavity, which has great potential for applications that require precise control of the heating area.

articleTitle: A 2-Bit Metasurface Design for Millimeter-Wave Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This paper proposes a 2-bit millimeter-wave metasurface unit with ultra-wide-angle stability, where the reflection characteristics are controlled by manipulating two PIN diodes embedded in the unit. The unit's center frequency is 28.5 GHz, with a 2-bit phase operation range spanning 28.25-28.75 GHz. The unit exhibits excellent angular stability, maintaining superior amplitude and phase performance under oblique incidence of plane waves up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 75^{\circ}$</tex> in the E-plane <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varphi=90^{\circ})$</tex>. By employing an optimal arrangement method for directive beam metasurfaces, the proposed units were arrayed into a 16-by-16 meta surface. At the center frequency, the meta surface achieved beam scanning of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 65^{\circ}$</tex> in the E-plane <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varphi=90^{\circ})$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 60^{\circ}$</tex> in the H-plane <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varphi=0^{\circ})$</tex>, with a peak maximum gain of 24.28 dBi and an aperture efficiency of 23.28%. The -1 dB gain bandwidth covers the range from 28 GHz to 29 GHz.

articleTitle: Modification of the Shaft-Rate Magnetic Field Model Based on Random Sea Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: The frequency of the ship's shaft-rate magnetic field is between 1 and 7 Hz, exhibiting clear line spectral characteristics, which represent an important signal characteristic of the ship. In order to study the propagation and distribution characteristics of the ship's shaft-rate magnetic field and to create a more accurate model for analysis, this paper employs the finite element method to construct a ship's shaft-rate magnetic field model based on finite elements. This model simulates the random sea surface and analyses the vertical spatial distribution of the shaft-rate magnetic field as well as the attenuation characteristics. Finally, a comparative analysis is conducted using the actual measured data at sea. The findings demonstrate that the finite element model is capable of calculating the spatial distribution and attenuation characteristics of the various components of the shaft-rate magnetic field. When compared to the measured data, the model incorporating a random sea surface can more accurately simulate the shaft-rate magnetic field signal in an actual marine environment than the model with a flat sea surface. This results in an improvement in simulation accuracy from 73.95% to 82.98%.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Magnetic Field Sensing Technology in Power System State Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: The application research of magnetic field sensing technology in power system status monitoring is increasingly receiving attention. By utilizing highly sensitive magnetic field sensors, the operational status and safety of power equipment can be monitored in real-time, thereby improving the reliability and stability of the power system. The fiber optic magnetic field sensor proposed in this article has the advantages of a wide measurement range, passive measurement characteristics, no need to replace the sensor battery, and no induction power supply, meeting the development requirements of low-carbon power systems.

articleTitle: A Graviton Model Based on Transient Annihilation and Regeneration of Positron Pairs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This paper introduces a hypothetical model that explores the instantaneous annihilation and regeneration of transient positron pairs within the Planck time frame. These virtual particles are posited as potential analogues or substitutes for gravitons, which remain elusive in quantum gravity theories. Utilizing complex scalar field theory, the paper constructs a mathematical framework that captures the rapid density fluctuations experienced by these particles. Through theoretical derivations and conceptual analyses, the proposed model examines the dynamics of these fleeting entities on the Planck scale and their implications for gravitational phenomena. In addition, the model may offer new insights into electromagnetic interactions by simulating the instantaneous annihilation and regeneration of positron pairs. Although grounded in speculation and not verifiable by current experiments, this study broadens the theoretical landscape by providing a novel approach to quantum gravity and opens avenues for future research. Its relevance to cosmology, particle physics, and electromagnetism is underscored, laying a theoretical foundation for potential experimental tests.

articleTitle: Water Cooling Design of Coil in Electromagnetic Separator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: The electromagnetic separation method is to obtain the best method of hightech stability isotope. It has the advantages of good generalability, high single separation coefficient, and strong flexibility. The electromagnetic separation method to implement the dependent device is an electromagnetic separator. The most critical and most costeffective system in the electromagnetic separator is the magnetic system. The magnetic system is mainly composed of magnets and coils. The design of the coil mainly includes mechanical shape design, amnad design, cooling design, etc., which are restricted and associated with each other. Recently, the Chinese Atomic Energy Science Research Institute has built two new-as-the-place electromagnetic separators. Among them The lower temperature rise is still within 2 degrees Celsius. This article will mainly introduce the water - cooled design process of two new electromagnetic separators and the final results.

articleTitle: A Radio Map Estimation Method Based on Improved Conditional Variational Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: A radio map is a specialized representation that depicts the power spectral density across a specific region. By leveraging electromagnetic maps, the efficient utilization of spectrum resources can be greatly enhanced. To achieve high-precision reconstruction of electromagnetic maps, this study proposes a method based on Conditional Variational Autoencoders (CVAE). This approach utilizes the redundancy in image information by incorporating both the values of sampled points and their positional data as conditions. The latent space is then sampled to generate reconstructed maps. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance when compared to traditional interpolation techniques and conventional autoencoder models, offering significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: An Improved ESPRIT Algorithm for Scaling Extrapolation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: The traditional scale measurement method is strictly based on the scale transformation where the electrical dimension remains unchanged. However, it is difficult to implement due to the size of the darkroom quiet zone and the test frequency range. There is a scaling extrapolation method based on the scattering center model. Firstly, the scattering center parameters of the scale target are estimated by parameter estimation algorithms, then the parameters of the full-scale target are derived by parameter relation of the full-size and the scale target. Finally, the extrapolated RCS of the full-scale target is obtained by the scattering center model. However, this method is limited by the accuracy of scattering center estimation. In this paper, we propose an improved ESPRIT algorithm, which is suitable for use in extrapolation methods and effectively reduces the error of the extrapolation method.

articleTitle: Research on Magnetic Field Sensing and Data Fusion Technology in Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: The research on magnetic field sensing and data fusion technology in the power system aims to enhance the monitoring and management capabilities of the power system. With the continuous growth of electricity demand, traditional monitoring methods are no longer able to meet the requirements of real-time and accuracy. In response to this challenge, magnetic field sensing technology has received widespread attention due to its high sensitivity and non-contact measurement advantages. By combining data fusion technology, multiple sources of information can be effectively integrated to achieve comprehensive monitoring and fault prediction of power equipment status. Research has shown that optimizing sensor layout and data processing algorithms can not only improve the reliability and safety of the system, but also provide solid technical support for the intelligent development of the power system. The combination of magnetic field sensing and data fusion has opened up new directions for innovative applications in the field of power, and has important academic value and practical significance.

articleTitle: Small-Target Infrastructure Detection with Spatial Tracking and Multi-Level Feature Extraction of Railway Track Scenes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: In the field of railway transportation, with the continuous improvement of train running speed and the continuous increase of operating mileage, it becomes particularly important to ensure the safety and integrity of small-target infrastructure along the railway train. Although many small-target detection methods have been proposed, the research on small-target infrastructure detection along rail trains is very rare. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a small-target infrastructure detection network with spatial tracking and multi-level feature extraction based on Yolov8n. The experimental results show that ST-YOLO has a 3.6% mAP improvement on the OSDaR23 dataset compared to the baseline Yolov8n, and shows significant advantages over other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Tunable Metasurface Unit with Dual Functionality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This paper introduces a dual-functional broadband reconfigurable metasurface unit that integrates reflection and absorption capabilities. The unit adopts the coupling mode of square metal patch layer and side metal column, which allows for flexible switching of its electromagnetic response characteristics by adjusting the bias current through control diodes. Simulation results demonstrate that, for reflection performance, within the 6.973GHz to 12.104GHz range (53.8% relative bandwidth), the unit's reflection amplitude is consistently greater than -1.1dB, while the reflection phase difference is stably maintained within a range of 180°±20°. For absorption performance, within the 7.20GHz to 12.13GHz range, the unit's reflection amplitude is consistently less than -10dB. The unit operates across the entire x-band frequency range (8GHz to 12GHz), making it effective for beam steering and absorption.

articleTitle: Design of Reconfigurable Symmetrical Double-Beam Holographic Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: In this paper, the influence of reflected wave on the radiation performance of holographic antenna is analyzed, and a double-beam holographic antenna is designed. The proposed antenna etches slots on the SIW waveguide and loads PIN diodes to achieve dynamic modulation. By introducing a reflected wave through a short circuit at the end of the waveguide, the reflected wave excites the holographic surface of the incident wave to generate a beam direction that is symmetric about the Z-axis. The proposed antenna is excited by a single feeding and shares the same aperture, and has the characteristics of simple structure and high aperture efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Network Convergence Architecture Design and Optimization for Satellite Communications Combined with 5G
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This paper discusses the network architecture design and optimization for the convergence of satellite communications and 5G, aiming to build an integrated network with seamless coverage to achieve the advantages of wide-area coverage and efficient bearer. By analyzing the convergence application scenarios, such as hybrid multicast, kiosk and cell backhaul, this paper proposes a network architecture scheme for the convergence of satellite communications and 5G, emphasizing the importance of network integrity and lightweight design. The specific scheme includes the cooperative work of the ground centralized control center, satellite terminals and satellite mobile core network. In order to optimize the network performance, this paper proposes a number of optimization strategies, such as network delay processing, redundancy coverage and area division, and verifies the effectiveness of the scheme through simulation analysis. The study shows that the optimized network architecture can significantly reduce the network packet loss rate and access user delay, improve the overall communication quality, and provide an important reference for the future development of communication networks.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of the Electromagnetic Pulse Effect on an Electronic Governor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic destruction effect of a typical electronic governor is investigated by means of pulsed current inj ection. Firstly, the working principle of electronic governor (ESC) is introduced, and then pulse current injection experiments are carried out with pulse amplitude and injection port as independent variables to obtain the damage threshold and damage mode of electronic governor. The threshold of the signal output port is 140A, and the threshold of the power input port is 160A. The damage mode is mainly serious degradation and direct damage. And it was found that the damaging components of the ESC were NMOS tubes, current sampling amplifiers and pre-drivers etc.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on the Echo-Signal Modeling of Sea-Targets Based on Semi-Deterministic Facet Scattering Model with Shooting-Bouncing Ray
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: On the basis of the scattering center method (SCM), the semi-deterministic facet scattering model (SDFSM) and the shooting-bouncing ray (SBR) method are used to establish two types of radar echo-signal simulation models (RESSM) for composite scenarios of sea-targets in this paper, namely the delay model and the spectrum model. Furthermore, the linear frequency modulated continuous wave (LFMCW) was used as input to simulate the RESSM of a quasi-static composite scenario of a sea-target, respectively by two models. The radar echo amplitude distribution is counted, and the one-dimensional high resolution range profile (HRRP) are respectively computed, which verifies the accuracy of the two methods.

articleTitle: A Hybrid 2.5D T-matrix Extraction Technique for Efficient Field Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: The complexity in electromagnetic scatterers has grown significantly over the past few decades. Traditional approaches for modeling their scattering characteristics often depend on full-wave simulations or analytical techniques limited to regular geometries. These methods, however, are inefficient and not suitable for optimizing and designing complex structures nor for simulation in large spaces. This paper introduces a novel 2.5D T-matrix extraction method designed for scatterers with arbitrary shapes. The approach facilitates efficient simulation of electromagnetic structures with complex geometries and configurations. The extraction process leverages vector cylinder wave expansions combined with numerical simulations of surface fields, minimizing computational overhead and addressing the limitations of conventional methods when handling irregular shapes. To validate the proposed method, several numerical examples involving scatterers of varying shapes are presented and compared against full-wave simulation results.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Computational Modeling and Bistatic Scattering Characteristics Analysis of Spherical Jammer Group
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: Bistatic radar is widely used in the military field with its good anti-jammer ability and accurate detection and identification ability. How to implement effective jammer for this kind of radar system has become a research hotspot at present. Due to the small scattering intensity and weak echo energy of j ammer monomer, it has no advantage in countering the bistatic radar. It is necessary to release multiple jammers to form a group to form strong scattering, so as to interfere with the bistatic radar to detect and recognize the target, so the study on the scattering characteristics of the jammer group is particularly important. Therefore, this paper takes the group composed of spherical monomer as an example, first of all, MATLAB and CST STUDIO SUITE (CST) are used for joint modeling, and then electromagnetic simulation calculation is carried out on the group of spherical jammer objects with different bands, different sphere sizes, different group densities and different group distributions to analyze the bistatic scattering characteristics under different parameters. The research results show that the four parameters will have different degrees of influence on the bistatic scattering characteristics of the spherical jammer group, which provides a theoretical basis and data support for parameter selection and airspace planning against the bistatic radar.

articleTitle: Improving the Performance of the Ryu SDN Controller Through Multi-Threading
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: Software-Defined Networks (SDN) fundamentally transform traditional network architecture. However, the performance of SDN controllers, particularly in their single-threaded implementations like Ryu, poses a major challenge for large-scale environments. This paper proposes an innovative multi-threaded architecture to enhance the performance of the Ryu controller. Our approach enables efficient parallel management of network events without requiring major changes to the source code. Experimental tests conducted with the Cbench tool demonstrate significant performance improvements, with a 174% increase in throughput (from 2112.30 to 5791.66 flows per second) and a notable reduction in latency. This solution addresses the growing demands of modern network infrastructures while maintaining compatibility with existing applications.

articleTitle: SMART-AGRI-TCHAD: An Integrated IoT-SDR Architecture for Smart Agriculture in Arid Zones
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: In this article, we propose an innovative smart agriculture solution for the arid regions of Chad, where approximately 80% of the population depends on subsistence farming. Our approach integrates four complementary technologies: the Internet of Things (IoT) for environmental data collection, the MQTT protocol for efficient communication over limited bandwidth, Software-Defined Radio (SDR) technology for flexible connectivity in rural areas, and the Fledge platform for data analysis and processing. The proposed architecture includes a containerized infrastructure that facilitates deployment and maintenance, as well as a real-time alert system via Slack. Performance tests demonstrate the viability of our solution, with data rates reaching 37.94 Mb/s. This approach enables more efficient water resource management and improved agricultural productivity in areas facing major climatic challenges. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of our solution for environmental monitoring and real-time decision-making in the context of agriculture in arid regions.

articleTitle: Perimeter Security Monitoring of Small Sample $\Phi-{}$OTDR Based on Multi-Scale Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: Distributed optical fiber vibration sensing technology based on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi$</tex>-OTDR principle holds significant application value in the field of perimeter security monitoring. However, in practical applications, the limited number of target event samples presents a small-sample challenge, restricting the performance and generalizability of monitoring systems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a method that achieves high classification accuracy for signal classification tasks involving four typical intrusion events under small-sample conditions. Experimental validation was conducted using field-collected data, and the results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve high classification precision and event recognition rates even with small sample sizes. This provides an effective solution for optical fiber-based perimeter security monitoring in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Telemetry Antenna Based on Electromagnetic Vortex Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: The existing telemetry technology is unable to meet the growing demand for high-speed and high-capacity transmission of flight test telemetry data. As the front-end of telemetry systems for transmitting and receiving signals, the role of telemetry antennas cannot be ignored. By combining telemetry antenna design technology with Orbital angular momentum (OAM) electromagnetic vortex technology, a telemetry antenna based on telemetry C-band can be proposed. The results show that this telemetry antenna can stably generate multiple modes of OAM beams within the working frequency band, and the beams have good rotation and symmetry, confirming its effectiveness and feasibility. Exploring new telemetry antenna technologies in the new telemetry frequency band can achieve integration and miniaturization of telemetry antennas, and to a certain extent, improve spectrum utilization.

articleTitle: STIR/SHAKEN: Implementation of a Robust Authentication Mechanism for Securing Public Health Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: In a context where the security of public health communications is becoming crucial, this research presents an innovative implementation of the STIR/SHAKEN protocol to fight against the proliferation of fraudulent calls and medical misinformation. Faced with alarming statistics revealing about 20 billion spam calls in the first half of 2024, our study proposes a robust authentication solution based on an Asterisk architecture adapted to the medical sector. The adopted methodology is based on a rigorous digital certification process, allowing for the systematic verification of the authenticity of SIP calls. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the system, particularly through the distinction between authenticated (number 1001) and non-compliant (number 1024) calls, with systematic blocking of suspicious communications. Our approach stands out from existing solutions due to its specific adaptation to the challenges of public health and its ability to effectively protect sensitive medical communications. This contribution provides a concrete response to the security challenges of health communications, while paving the way for future improvements incorporating emerging technologies for even more robust protection of digital health systems.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Sensor Data Fusion for Smart Elderly Care Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: Against the backdrop of increasing demand for elderly care, elderly care robots play a special role. Currently, the multi-sensor data fusion in elderly care robots faces issues such as low accuracy of sensor data collection and the need for optimization and innovation in fusion algorithms. To address these issues, this paper optimizes the fusion algorithm that combines the Kalman filter algorithm, artificial neural network (ANN) algorithm, and SVM algorithm. First, raw data is collected from the sensors of the elderly care robot, checked, cleaned, and reprocessed using min-max normalization. Then, the Kalman filter performs preliminary data processing, state prediction, and calculates relevant parameters to reduce noise and uncertainty, improving accuracy. Next, the artificial neural network receives the filtered data, proportionally divides the data set, selects ReLU and linear activation functions for the hidden layer and output layer respectively, uses mean squared error as the loss function, and updates weights using back propagation and stochastic gradient descent algorithms to input data into the fusion to obtain feature vectors. Finally, SVM uses this vector as input, trains the model with labeled data, inputs the newly collected and processed sensor data into the model for prediction, and adjusts parameters based on the results to achieve final fusion and decision-making. An experimental environment is established in nursing homes or senior living communities, and comparative tests with other fusion algorithms show that this algorithm has greater advantages in the accurate collection of sensor data for elderly care robots.

articleTitle: Aperiodic 3D Folded Metamaterial and Defected Ground Structures to Enhance Isolation of Miniaturized MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel miniaturized 3D folded metamaterial structure, combined with a segmented and defected ground optimization method, to design a compact, low-profile Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna with low coupling and high isolation. The 3D folded metamaterial utilizes the upper and lower metal layers of the dielectric substrate, folding the traditional metamaterial in half to achieve miniaturization. Additionally, the MIMO antenna system incorporates a defected ground structure to reduce electromagnetic wave reflection and scattering, leveraging the three-dimensional ground defect space to integrate the 3D folded metamaterial. The physical dimensions of the aperiodic 3D folded metamaterial are determined through a segmented optimization method. By utilizing the filtering characteristics of the metamaterial, a dual-band, dual-element MIMO antenna system is realized with high integration, high isolation, low coupling, and low return loss. Simulation results indicate that the antenna model demonstrates strong performance in the commonly used frequency band of 5.43 – 5.52 GHz, with an antenna spacing of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.1}\ \lambda$</tex>, characterized by low return loss and high isolation. The effectiveness of the proposed design is validated through fabrication and testing.

articleTitle: Multi-Physics Field Simulation of Dual Microwave Coaxial Linear Plasma
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: A large-area and uniformly distributed plasma is significant for microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition (MPCVD). In this research, argon was utilized as the working gas to create a large-area, high-density, and evenly distributed microwave coaxial linear plasma. The simulation is used to determine the effects of varying power and gas pressure on the electron density and electron temperature of the plasma. The results of the simulation demonstrate that the distribution area of the high-density plasma gradually expands as the microwave power or gas pressure increases. The high-density plasma expands to the majority of the reaction chamber when the power is greater than 1200W (gas pressure 80Pa) or the gas pressure is granter than 160Pa (power 800W), and the axial electron density and electron temperature are on the same order of magnitude. On this basis, this paper further proposes a method of two-way microwave-excited plasma. The majority of the reaction chamber's volume is filled with high-density plasma when the microwave power of each way reaches 800W (air pressure 80Pa), and the electron density and electron temperature in the axial direction are uniformly distributed.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Hop Path Optimization of UAV Based on Quality Factor and Neo4j
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: With the wide application of UAVs in military, how to ensure stable communication link in harsh environment becomes an important problem. Especially under the influence of electronic interference and complex terrain, a single UAV cannot provide reliable communication. To solve this problem, a multi-hop communication path optimization method based on quality factor and Neo4j knowledge graph is proposed in this paper. The method considers the signal strength, spectrum utilization, interference, modulation mode and other factors, sets the quality factor to evaluate the path, and uses the Neo4j graph database to calculate the optimal communication path efficiently. By setting the threshold reasonably and optimizing the path selection, the throughput, connectivity and anti-interference ability of the multi-hop communication network are significantly improved. The experimental results show that this method can effectively improve the communication throughput in most cases, especially in complex environments, showing good performance and reliability.

articleTitle: The Joint Radar Cross Section Imaging and Inversion Method Based on Modified Backprojection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: High stealth property is the core performance of modern weapons and equipment. In general, radar cross section (RCS) is used to represent the steal performance. The RCS imaging and inversion play an important role in evaluating the steal performance of modern weapons and equipment. In this paper, the principle of two-dimensional RCS imaging is introduced firstly. Then, the RCS imaging and inversion method based on modified backprojection algorithm is proposed. The joint RCS imaging and inversion method are both verified by simulation experiments. The results show that the proposed method has high accuracy.

articleTitle: Filtering Dense Dielectric Patch Antenna with a Pair of Step Arc-Shaped Slots
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel dense dielectric patch antenna (DDPA) with a flltering function, featuring an arc-shaped silver-plated patch. The antenna is composed of a dense dielectric patch (DDP) and a dual-layer PCB. A pair of stepped arc-shaped slots are designed on the DDP, which confines the resonant field region of the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode mainly to the area inside the stepped arc-shaped slot. As a result, the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode resonant frequency shifts to a higher frequency, forming a passband with the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> mode. The arc-shaped part in the middle of the DDP is silver-plated, altering the original electric field distribution and introducing a radiation zero at the lower frequency edge of the passband. By loading parallel crossed stubs onto the microstrip line, the interference in the high-frequency stopband is effectively suppressed. Therefore, this filtering antenna achieves a filtering function without requiring additional filtering circuits. Simulation results indicate that the antenna provides a relative bandwidth of 14.8% within the passband (0.58 GHz, 3.62 GHz∼4.2 GHz) with an average gain of 6.37 dBi.

articleTitle: UWB and High-Gain Shaped Metal Jet Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: The shaped metal jet antenna is an emerging type of antenna and offers a novel concept for deformable antennas. However, this jet antenna, resembling a monopole antenna, also inherits the drawbacks of narrow bandwidth and poor directivity typical of monopole designs. To address these issues, this study introduces a conical base for the antenna, leveraging the ultra- wideband and high-gain characteristics of conical antennas. The design successfully integrates the advantages of both antenna types, expanding the bandwidth. Simulation results indicate that after incorporating the conical base, the antenna's operating range extended to 1–20 GHz, with a bandwidth improvement of over 15 times. Additionally, the antenna achieved a peak gain of 8.3 dBi within the usable frequency range, significantly advancing the practical engineering applications of shaped metal jet antennas.

articleTitle: Broadband Cavity Filter Using Coaxial Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This paper presents a metal cavity broadband bandpass filter, which incorporates two pairs of short-circuited metal cylinders within a cylindrical resonant cavity. Three independent resonant modes are excited in the resonant cavity to form a passband. The first two resonant modes are coaxial modes introduced by the added short-circuited metal cylinders, while the third resonant mode is a probe mode introduced by enhancing source-load coupling. The filter has a center frequency of 2.595 GHz and an absolute bandwidth of 610 MHz. A normalized coupling matrix of the filter was extracted using a comprehensive technical analysis method. The theoretical results derived from the coupling matrix were compared with HFSS full-wave simulation results, showing good agreement and confirming the design's validity.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference Attack Against Infrared Object Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: Infrared object detection systems, operate reliably in low-light and complex conditions by capturing thermal emissions playing a critical role in military, industrial, and rescue applications. This paper exploits vulnerabilities of infrared object detection systems under the electromagnetic interference (EMI) Attack. We propose a particle swarm optimization (PSO) method for rapid interference frequency identification and an amplitude modulation approach to target specific injection regions in the detector's field of view, allowing precise control over interference effects. Our experiments on a commercial infrared detector reveal high success rates in object-creation and object-hiding attacks, which achieve 94% and 99% successful rates respectively. We also discuss countermeasures to improve detection system resilience against EMI.

articleTitle: Detection of PCB Socket Defects: A Comparative Analysis of Transfer Learning, Semantic Segmentation and Feature Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: The reliability and functionality of electronic components are critically important for efficiency in industrial production. As one of the fundamental components, printed circuit boards (PCBs) playa crucial role in the operational performance of electronic devices. Any defects in PCBs can lead to operational disruptions and increased costs. Specifically, sockets where sensors are connected are among the most susceptible areas for defects, and accurate and effective detection of these defects is vital for maintaining product quality and operational efficiency. Traditional defect detection methods typically rely on manual inspections, which are time-consuming and prone to human error, limiting their reliability. Advances in machine learning and image processing offer promising alternatives for automated defect detection. In this study, the performances of transfer learning (Googlenet) and semantic segmentation (U-Net) were compared for the classification of socket defects on a PCB. The dataset used in the study was specifically created for this research. The performances of three different models Googlenet, Googlenet+Relieff, and U-Net were evaluated. The Googlenet+Relieff model was identified as the most successful with an impressive accuracy rate of 98.6% and a classification time of 0.274 seconds. This high success rate demonstrates the effectiveness of combining feature selection algorithms with transfer learning. The results indicate that transfer learning has significant potential for improving industrial quality control processes.

articleTitle: Application of DataLink in Joint Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: This article analyzes the application of data link technology in joint operations and its impact on modern warfare. DataLinks enhance the efficiency of information transmission, strengthen the ability of troops to coordinate operations, and improve the efficiency of situational awareness, command decision-making, and combat execution. The article discusses the classification, technical architecture of DataLink, and their key role in enhancing operational effectiveness, while also highlighting challenges such as security, interoperability, and the stability of information transmission. Finally, the article looks forward to the future development trends of data link technology, including the integration of artificial intelligence, the evolution of network-centric warfare, and the potential application of quantum communication technology, emphasizing the significant role of DataLink in promoting network-centric warfare and enhancing the effectiveness of joint operations.

articleTitle: Encoder-Decoder Based Complex-Valued Transformer for Signal Classification and Demodulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: In electronic communications, the capability to accurately demodulate signals is a cornerstone for effective data exchange. However, in adversarial or non-cooperative settings where system parameters are unknown, traditional demodulation techniques often fail to decode the complex waveform characteristics influenced by modulation and communication specifics. This paper introduces an novel solution—a complex-valued transformer with an encoder-decoder architecture specifically designed for the classification and demodulation of single-carrier signals. By leveraging the nuances of modulation, synchronization, and bit-level information embedded within I/Q data, our proposed model learns to discriminate and decode a plethora of communication signals through a unified transformer framework. This architecture encapsulates the complexities inherent in signal processing into an end-to-end trainable model, and demonstrates robust performance in both signal classification and blind demodulation scenarios. Our experimental findings confirm that this novel architecture not only excels in classifying single-carrier signals but also performs commendably in challenging conditions where demodulation occurs without prior knowledge of signal parameters which highlights it's potential as a versatile tool for communication systems operating under non-cooperative environments, offering significant advancements over traditional methods by providing concurrent classification and demodulation capabilities within a single forward pass.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Accelerometer Based on Cavity Optomechanical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: An accelerometer is an inertial sensor used to measure the magnitude of acceleration and vibration frequency of a moving object. It finds wide applications in fields such as aerospace, autonomous driving, and unmanned equipment to enable inertial navigation or inertial measurement. In traditional accelerometers, thermal noise has the greatest impact on detection accuracy. To effectively reduce thermal noise, this paper designs a novel accelerometer structure based on a cavity optomechanical system. The design was optimized through simulations using COMSOL software, which confirmed the structural validity of the proposed accelerometer. Additionally, the first-order modal frequency and linearity simulation results from COMSOL were verified using Simulink software, demonstrating the reasonableness of the results.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Maritime Radar Target Detection Method Based on Multi-Domain Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: Maritime radar is a crucial component of the Vessel Traffic Service (VTS) system, and sea clutter interference is a significant factor affecting the accuracy of radar target detection and tracking. To enhance the accuracy of maritime radar target detection, the spatiotemporal and time-frequency information in radar echoes are utilized, and a two-stage target detection method was developed. In the coarse stage, a detection process for rapidly extracting target candidate regions is designed by combining the phase and time-domain amplitude features. In the fine stage, four key features extracted from time-frequency domain are adopted, including Relative Average Amplitude (RAA), Temporal Hurst Exponent (THE), Sample Entropy (SE), and Doppler Peak Height (DPH). We use these features construct a fused feature space, subsequently, the feature pyramid is utilized to enhance feature representation capabilities across multiple scales. Finally, a simple and feasible decision tree algorithm is used to classify the fused feature space, distinguishing between sea clutter and targets. The empirical results demonstrate that compared with YOLOv8 and Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) detection methods, the proposed method increases accuracy to 93.2% while maintaining a recall rate of 89.2%.

articleTitle: Channel-Robust RF Fingerprint Authentication for LTE-V2X via Channel-Adversarial Siamese Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Communication, Sensing and Electromagnetics (ICSE)
abstract: Radio Frequency Fingerprinting (RFF) has emerged as a promising technique for physical-layer authentication, utilizing hardware-specific characteristics for secure identification. However, in L TE-based Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) systems, the high-speed mobility of vehicles and varying multipath channels introduce significant challenges to RFF reliability. This paper proposes a robust RFF extraction and authentication framework tailored for L TE V2X applications. In the extraction phase, Demodulation Reference Signal (DMRS)-based Channel State Information (CSI) is transformed in the logarithmic domain to enhance learning of device-specific features while minimizing channel interference. For authentication, we introduce a Channel-Adversarial Siamese Network (CASNet), which employs gradient reversal layers to map signal fingerprints from different channels into a unified feature space, improving recognition accuracy under diverse channel conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that CASNet significantly outperforms conventional methods, achieving high accuracy and stability across both stationary and mobile scenarios, proving effective for LTE V2X authentication in real-world environments.
